name: Pearl-white lacquer on steel (the Elan's pearl steel)
process: Pearl steel is the white of the Future: steel under a warm-white lacquer (RAL 1013, whose German name is Perlweiss, 'pearl white') carrying a silver-white pearl pigment, so the white has a soft inner lustre that brightens toward the specular and sparkles faintly up close. The pearl is made by platelets of mica (n about 1.5), 10-60 um across and about 0.5 um thick, coated with a thin film of titanium dioxide (n about 2.7); the film reflects by interference, and the platelets lie parallel to the surface, so the lustre follows the light like a mirror broken into flakes. Two builds are needed. Inside (the Atrium's twelve ribs, the Sphere's lattice and throat, the collar and the irises, the Hall of Light's frame and vault): the ribs are shop-painted like the Rotunda's lattice (blast-cleaned to Sa 2 1/2, an epoxy build coat), then a pearl basecoat and a satin clear. Outside (the dome's seamless shell, 22-36.3 m): the steel plates are welded, the welds ground, and the whole shell faired like a superyacht hull: epoxy fairing compound, a high-build epoxy surfacer sanded straight, then a white basecoat, the pearl, and a gloss clearcoat that gives depth and carries the UV; the hull painter's tolerance is under 0.5 mm over lines of 50-60 m.

angleShift.text: A thin-film interference colour shifts toward shorter wavelengths as the view turns toward grazing, so a silver-white pearl can cool faintly (bluish or lilac) at the silhouette while its face stays warm white.

angleShift.derivation: thin-film condition 2 n d cos(theta_t) = m lambda: at larger angles cos(theta_t) falls and the reflected peak moves to shorter lambda

familyNote.text: The owner's principles put pearl steel in the white family ('plaster, then limewash, then pearl steel'; 'Pearl-white lacquered steel, satin' as the Future's white), but the steel record is declared an accent of the glass family. A family belongs to a substance, so pearl steel is steel (accent of glass) in this working until the Architect decides; the look is the white family's.

photograph: A warm white with a soft, deep lustre that brightens toward the reflection of the sky and dims at the flanks; close up a fine glitter of flakes.
The shell, faired and clear-coated, mirrors the sky and the trees in long unbroken reflections, with no panel lines.
The interior ribs are satin: a broad soft highlight along each rib, no mirror.
